1	# Frade — Engineering Agent Contract
     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	This file defines repository-wide engineering rules for AI coding agents working on Frade.
     6	
     7	These rules are mandatory.
     8	
     9	Subsystem-specific rules may exist in nested `AGENTS.md` files and may impose stricter constraints.
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## 1. Development Method
    14	
    15	Frade uses:
    16	
    17	```text
    18	SDD / OpenSpec
    19	    ↓
    20	BDD
    21	    ↓
    22	TDD
    23	    ↓
    24	Implementation
    25	    ↓
    26	Verification
    27	    ↓
    28	Architecture Gate
    29	    ↓
    30	Archive
    31	```
    32	
    33	Implementation follows specification.
    34	
    35	Specification must not be silently changed to match implementation.
    36	
    37	Tests must not be weakened to make implementation pass.
    38	
    39	---
    40	
    41	## 2. OpenSpec Is the Change Authority
    42	
    43	For substantial product or architecture work:
    44	
    45	1. identify the active OpenSpec change;
    46	2. read its proposal/spec/design/tasks;
    47	3. validate the change before implementation;
    48	4. implement only the active scope;
    49	5. run required tests;
    50	6. run OpenSpec verification;
    51	7. pass the Architecture Gate;
    52	8. only then archive the change.
    53	
    54	Do not implement a later dependent change before the previous change has passed its gate.
    55	
    56	---
    57	
    58	## 3. STOP Conditions
    59	
    60	Stop progression whenever any of the following is true:
    61	
    62	```text
    63	required test fails
    64	typecheck fails in affected code
    65	OpenSpec validation fails
    66	OpenSpec verification has a correctness blocker
    67	architecture invariant fails
    68	architecture gate fails
    69	reference parity fails
    70	a specification conflict exists
    71	a previously fixed regression reappears
    72	```
    73	
    74	Resolve the blocker before moving to the next phase.
    75	
    76	---
    77	
    78	## 4. No Patch-Loop Rule
    79	
    80	After two unsuccessful fixes of the same deterministic defect:
    81	
    82	```text
    83	STOP PATCHING
    84	```
    85	
    86	Before another production-code modification, perform root-cause analysis.
    87	
    88	Classify the failure as:
    89	
    90	```text
    91	DOMAIN_MODEL
    92	INVARIANT
    93	ALGORITHM
    94	ABSTRACTION_BOUNDARY
    95	STATE_TRANSITION
    96	TEST
    97	SPEC_CONFLICT
    98	INTEGRATION
    99	ENVIRONMENT
   100	```
   101	
   102	Do not continue making local symptom-oriented fixes.
   103	
   104	---
   105	
   106	## 5. Regression-First Rule
   107	
   108	For a reproduced defect use:
   109	
   110	```text
   111	DEFECT
   112	 ↓
   113	DETERMINISTIC REPRODUCTION
   114	 ↓
   115	FAILING TEST / FIXTURE
   116	 ↓
   117	ROOT CAUSE
   118	 ↓
   119	IMPLEMENTATION FIX
   120	 ↓
   121	TARGETED TEST
   122	 ↓
   123	FULL REGRESSION SUITE
   124	```
   125	
   126	Do not fix production code first and add a regression test afterwards unless reproduction before the fix is technically impossible and explicitly documented.
   127	
   128	---
   129	
   130	## 6. Test Integrity
   131	
   132	Do not make tests pass by weakening them.
   133	
   134	Forbidden without an explicit specification decision:
   135	
   136	```text
   137	test.skip
   138	it.skip
   139	describe.skip
   140	
   141	test.only
   142	it.only
   143	describe.only
   144	
   145	removing meaningful assertions
   146	loosening geometry tolerances
   147	blind snapshot regeneration
   148	deleting regression fixtures
   149	ignoring thrown errors
   150	changing expected values merely to match current implementation
   151	@ts-nocheck
   152	@ts-ignore
   153	```
   154	
   155	Existing regression tests are historical evidence.
   156	
   157	Do not remove them casually.
   158	
   159	---
   160	
   161	## 7. Architecture Direction
   162	
   163	Prefer dependency direction:
   164	
   165	```text
   166	UI / Framework
   167	      ↓
   168	Adapters
   169	      ↓
   170	Application / Interaction
   171	      ↓
   172	Domain
   173	      ↓
   174	Pure primitives
   175	```
   176	
   177	Do not solve domain defects inside renderers, React lifecycle hooks, persistence adapters, or framework glue.
   178	
   179	Fix the first incorrect decision in the proper layer.
   180	
   181	---
   182	
   183	## 8. Derived State
   184	
   185	Do not persist state that can be deterministically derived from semantic state unless the specification explicitly requires materialization.
   186	
   187	Typical transient/derived state includes:
   188	
   189	```text
   190	selection handles
   191	preview geometry
   192	render-only paths
   193	cached projections
   194	temporary interaction coordinates
   195	```
   196	
   197	---
   198	
   199	## 9. Determinism
   200	
   201	Core domain algorithms must not depend on accidental runtime state such as:
   202	
   203	```text
   204	Math.random()
   205	Date.now()
   206	DOM ordering
   207	React render ordering
   208	screen zoom
   209	devicePixelRatio
   210	pointer event frequency
   211	animation-frame timing
   212	```
   213	
   214	Identical semantic inputs must produce identical semantic outputs within the explicitly defined numeric tolerance.
   215	
   216	---
   217	
   218	## 10. Scope Discipline
   219	
   220	Do not turn an active OpenSpec change into an unrelated repository-wide refactoring.
   221	
   222	If unrelated technical debt is discovered:
   223	
   224	```text
   225	document it
   226	do not opportunistically implement it
   227	```
   228	
   229	unless it blocks the active change.
   230	
   231	---
   232	
   233	## 11. Evidence
   234	
   235	Never report:
   236	
   237	```text
   238	"should pass"
   239	"looks correct"
   240	"probably fixed"
   241	```
   242	
   243	as verification.
   244	
   245	Claims about passing tests or validation must come from commands that were actually executed.
   246	
   247	At the end of implementation report:
   248	
   249	```text
   250	CHANGE:

1	# Frade common agent workflow — v1.1
     2	
     3	These mandatory rules apply to every engineering branch/worktree of this Frade repository. The user's 1 October 2026 instruction authorizes automatic independent OpenAI Codex review of relevant Frade sources, contracts, tests and evidence. Credentials, secrets, global settings and other repositories are excluded. Existing AGENTS, approved OpenSpec scope, STOP conditions, test integrity, frozen controls and each numbered checkpoint remain mandatory.
     4	
     5	## Automatic PRE and POST
     6	
     7	The owning agent reads its approved branch plan, selects the exact model and reasoning effort assigned to the current stage and PRE/POST review role, prepares the relevant packet/prompt, invokes a fresh independent reviewer and receives the result without human relay or repeated review approval. There is no universal model/effort default, silent upgrade or downgrade. Do not reuse implementation or fix-worker parameters for a review unless that role is explicitly assigned in the plan. Missing, ambiguous or conflicting assignment, unavailable required model/effort or unverified sandbox is BLOCKED for the actual decision/limitation. Record the stage, role and exact selected plan path/hash/excerpt. Requested model/effort and independently attested backend/effort are separate; actual backend/effort remains NOT_CONFIRMED.
     8	
     9	Use this order: approved coherent proposal/design/spec/tasks → actual strict validation → independent PRE PASS → BDD / meaningful RED → implementation → required GREEN/general checks → OpenSpec verify → independent POST PASS → archive/checkpoint. Preserve stricter program gates and original origin. A focused PASS does not close cumulative work, grant visual acceptance, waive a failed test or authorize the next numbered change. A machine gate is not independent approval. FAIL stops its scope. Human decisions are required for material scope/spec/visual/destination or unresolved authorization/environment changes, not for passing prompts/results.
    10	
    11	The reviewer receives an immutable minimal explicit packet. Missing relevant inputs are a completeness blocker. The authenticated external harness uses the signed-in account; auth is not copied or readable by reviewer commands. The pinned current-host runtime is Codex CLI 0.159.3 under WSL Ubuntu-22.04_E. Each invocation first runs an offline sandbox canary: packet read allowed; candidate, Git common storage, another worktree, auth/config reads denied; file writes and socket access denied. Network/apps/web/shell inheritance are disabled inside commands. Root deny with minimal public tools and explicit runtime read is mandatory, not just a read-only label.
    12	
    13	Generated instances also use `--ignore-user-config`, `--ignore-rules`, `project_doc_max_bytes=0`, `project_doc_fallback_filenames=[]`. Relevant AGENTS are selected explicitly in the packet. These suppress automatic AGENTS/rules/user-config loading; they do not remove platform instructions or built-in tool descriptions. Do not claim an unattested absence of all platform context. Credentials remain outside sandbox in the launcher. Missing or failed confinement/version proof is BLOCKED; no Windows fallback with weaker isolation.
    14	
    15	## Shared service discovery
    16	
    17	One installation lives in the repository's **Git common directory**, not a feature branch. `frade-workflow/current.json` points to an immutable content-hash release. It contains reviewed public policy, CLI and exact transport templates, no account configuration. No per-branch reviewer/model setup is needed. Each run derives the owning root/branch from actual cwd, verifies registration against this original Frade common directory, rejects unrelated repositories even if origin matches, and uses a unique run directory. Never run concurrent feature writers in one checkout.
    18	
    19	From any registered Frade worktree, in PowerShell:
    20	
    21	```powershell
    22	$fradeCommon = (git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir).Trim()
    23	$fradePointer = Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $fradeCommon 'frade-workflow/current.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
    24	$fradeRelease = Join-Path $fradeCommon ("frade-workflow/releases/" + $fradePointer.release)
    25	$fradeRunner = Join-Path $fradeRelease 'scripts/agent-review/cli.mjs'
    26	node $fradeRunner status
    27	Get-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $fradeRelease 'docs/engineering/agent-workflow.md') -Raw
    28	```
    29	
    30	`status` verifies every public bundle file before reporting AVAILABLE. The pointer digest must equal the verified returned release digest. If missing/drifted, stop and report BLOCKED; never fall back to a different repository/worktree. Older branch files and already-running chats cannot be silently rewritten/reinstructed. Load this shared policy through the one-time owner handoff; adopt tracked rules through that branch's approved control process. Future branches acquire root rules by adopting the process commit. No full UI merge is necessary.
    31	
    32	## Packet and owner adoption
    33	
    34	Before freeze, the owner selects root/scoped AGENTS, active artifacts, applicable contracts, source/tests/evidence and actual check records. Never send .git, .env, credential files, global settings or another repository. Secret/path guards, safe relative paths and raw file realpath checks are mandatory. Index must be empty; commit the authorized planning checkpoint when required, not by discarding/stashing unrelated work.
    35	
    36	An older branch saves exact reviewed public policy and necessary public controls from the shared release into its **own approved process evidence directory**, records release/version/origin/bytes/hashes, and selects those adopted relative paths. The runner requires a `policyArtifact` selected in `paths`, with bytes matching the shared policy SHA. This is task evidence, not per-branch model/account configuration. The supplier does not write active foreign checkouts. The consumer owns adoption/control compatibility revalidation, preserves its frozen origin and historical FAIL, and never broadens an allowlist or moves baseline silently.
    37	
    38	Select canonical CLI model ID and one exact effort from the approved plan; preserve plan naming/aliases in the exact source excerpt and make the mapping reviewable. The runner verifies safe ID/effort, phase, selected source raw SHA256 and excerpt; the owner and independent reviewer verify semantic approval and conflicts using complete relevant plan inputs. Request metadata is never its own approval. Original v3 templates retain historic constants only as immutable substitution origins. New generated CLI, probe policy, inner metadata and strict outer receipt must match the selected pair exactly.
    39	
    40	Prepare an external JSON request as task input (not inside the frozen candidate). This illustrative Sol/high pair belongs only to the example stage; replace every value from the actual approved stage assignment:
    41	
    42	```json
    43	{
    44	  "phase": "PRE",
    45	  "change": "selected-owning-change",
    46	  "scope": "Exact approved scope and exclusions",
    47	  "reviewPolicy": {
    48	    "stage": "example-stage",
    49	    "phase": "PRE",
    50	    "model": "gpt-6-sol",
    51	    "reasoningEffort": "high",
    52	    "source": {
    53	      "path": "openspec/changes/selected-owning-change/design.md",
    54	      "sha256": "<lowercase SHA256 of raw plan bytes>",
    55	      "excerpt": "<exact approved stage reviewer assignment from the plan>"
    56	    }
    57	  },
    58	  "policyArtifact": "openspec/changes/selected-owning-change/evidence/shared-policy.md",
    59	  "paths": ["AGENTS.md", "openspec/changes/selected-owning-change/design.md", "openspec/changes/selected-owning-change/evidence/shared-policy.md"],
    60	  "prompt": "Full prepared independent review prompt; list authority, scope, applicability, actual evidence, limits and require exactly one standalone GATE_STATUS: PASS or FAIL."
    61	}
    62	```
    63	
    64	The paths and placeholder hash/excerpt above only illustrate shape; the owner must include all necessary relevant inputs. Invoke and receive automatically:
    65	
    66	```powershell
    67	node $fradeRunner probe C:/path/to/external-request.json
    68	node $fradeRunner run C:/path/to/external-request.json
    69	```
    70	
    71	Old requests without an explicit valid reviewPolicy fail BLOCKED; status reports that plan selection is required, not a configured reviewer pair. A probe uses the same explicit selection and never chooses a reviewer default. The previously delivered Routing handoff remains unchanged at the user's request; this v1.1 rule supersedes only its obsolete universal Astra/xhigh wording. The Routing owner already received the direct correction and retains its control/adoption gates.
    72	
    73	The runner preserves full input selection, request/prompt, source/packet/instance hashes, full tracked and nonignored-untracked candidate bytes plus Git identity, stdout/stderr/exit/report and immutable receipt in its unique common run. Do not update sources, dashboards, index or HEAD during review. A changed candidate/request/packet/toolchain/release, failed execution, incomplete stream or ambiguous verdict is BLOCKED. Only a clean completed stream and one exact single-line verdict may authorize progression. The strict outer receipt overrides a permissive inner v3 result. Raw FAIL is never rewritten. Save the received outputs and provenance in dated owning evidence after unfreeze. Exit0=PASS, exit1=FAIL, exit2=BLOCKED; inspect receipt, not an isolated plausible sentence.
    74	
    75	## Required branch progress
    76	
    77	Every active engineering branch MUST maintain its own **tracked `*-STATUS.md`**. Retain existing program files: UI uses `docs/ui/UI-DESIGN-CONTRACT-STATUS.md`, Routing uses `docs/routing-v2/ROUTING-V2-STATUS.md`; otherwise use `docs/engineering/BRANCH-STATUS.md`. Do not create a shared feature-progress file in common storage.
    78	
    79	Include actual branch/worktree, active change, original baseline/cumulative origin and current checkpoint, phase, full stage list plus detailed active tasks, actual check/gate PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED/NOT_RUN, evidence/limitations, unresolved decisions/blockers, next action and commit/push state. Use UTC timestamps for evidence, optional MSK display.
    80	
    81	The owner refreshes on start/resume, accepted scope, completed/blocked tasks, completed check batch, PRE/POST receipt, blocker/visual decision, verify, archive, commit and verified publication. Defer dashboard writes while candidate is frozen. Open the file in the right panel; queued is not proof of visibility. Dashboard is a current projection, never approval/evidence replacement. Preserve historical dated evidence unchanged.
    82	
    83	## Checkpoints and parallel features
    84	
    85	Commit completed authorized checkpoints honestly, including explicitly incomplete FAIL checkpoints. Push only to a user-authorized remote/ref, verify actual remote SHA, never force or rewrite unrelated work. Publishing a UI checkpoint does not authorize publishing another branch. Serialize shared-file merges and explain conflicts.
    86	
    87	UI and Routing have independent feature gates. A directed product dependency exists only when a consumer uses supplier API/artifact/behavior. The consumer owns integration/waiting/adoption; the supplier does not wait for its gate/archive/process repair. Common ancestry, root AGENTS or a historical whole-file fingerprint is not itself a product dependency. If presentation actually changes routing semantics, split it into Routing-owned work.
    88	
    89	## Installation and limitations
    90	
    91	Publish a reviewed public release only after supplier verification and independent POST PASS. `publish` checks original POST transport fingerprints, strict output, packet hashes and every selected release file; it never copies product sources. Save install/pointer/hash/primary-loader provenance and check discovery/confinement from both worktree contexts. Older active owner checkouts are not edited here. Other hosts need one verified runtime installation; unsupported hosts report BLOCKED. These engineering instructions are not GitHub branch protection or CI enforcement.
    92	
    93	Official config references: [configuration](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference), [AGENTS discovery](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md). Executed local probes, not documentation alone, establish current-host command confinement.

     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	Define a reviewable successor visual contract for migrated workbench surfaces without silently replacing the existing approved VS Code pilot.
     6	
     7	The user accepted the full WB-001 replacement text on 30 September 2026. The canonical accepted text is in `../../decisions/visual-contract.md`; authority, text hash and explicit supersession ownership are in `../../decisions/wb001-acceptance-2026-09-30.md`. The pilot archive/sync owner consumes that record; this change does not edit/archive the pilot. Acceptance does not approve migration baselines or replace independent PRE.
     8	
     9	## Archive provenance
    10	
    11	The Purpose above is preserved verbatim from the accepted delta. Its source-relative inline paths refer to the original change. Current canonical authority: [accepted WB-001 text](../../changes/archive/2026-09-30-frade-ui-design-contract/decisions/visual-contract.md) and [acceptance and successor ownership](../../changes/archive/2026-09-30-frade-ui-design-contract/decisions/wb001-acceptance-2026-09-30.md).
    12	
    13	## Requirements
    14	
    15	### Requirement: Explicit accepted visual transition
    16	
    17	An approved decision SHALL reconcile pilot WB-001 ownership before migrated surfaces use Frade guide v1.0 instead of exact VS Code Dark Modern colors/geometry. Non-migrated surfaces SHALL retain their existing contracts. Behavioral workbench requirements, diagram compatibility and historical evidence SHALL remain intact. A proposal or token PASS MUST NOT be treated as acceptance of visual migration.
    18

    20

    26	Each affected surface SHALL have actual runtime screenshots and interaction/accessibility evidence for approved themes, density, viewport, fonts and scale. Loading/error/dirty/empty coverage SHALL reflect real implemented capabilities. Screenshots from a mockup or historical run MUST NOT substitute for current runtime evidence.

    29

    31	- **THEN** the report records the executed command and environment error separately from UI defects and leaves screenshots BLOCKED

1	# ui-design-contract Specification
     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	Make Frade UI changes reviewable against one canonical design contract while preserving engineering checkpoints and domain behavior.
     6	
     7	## Requirements
     8	
     9	### Requirement: Canonical mandatory UI contract
    10	
    11	Every new or modified UI surface SHALL record guide version 1.0, applicable FDS/A11Y rules, approved scope, affected states/themes/densities and evidence. Canonical documentation and the additive AGENTS section MUST preserve existing rules. UI's own conflicts/applicable controls MUST be resolved before adoption; independent routing work MUST NOT be a UI predecessor. Documentation alone MUST NOT claim merge protection.
    12	
    13	#### Scenario: Independent frozen consumer control
    14	
    15	- **WHEN** routing freezes an earlier shared engineering contract and UI independently changes it within its own approved scope
    16	- **THEN** UI follows its own PRE, while routing owns its later adoption/revalidation without blocking UI
    17	
    18	#### Scenario: Actual UI contract conflict
    19	
    20	- **WHEN** UI violates its own approved visual/behavior contract or required check
    21	- **THEN** UI progression stops until that conflict/failure is resolved in its owning layer
    22	
    23	### Requirement: Independent feature process and consumer dependencies
    24	
    25	UI Contract SHALL use its own baseline, feature workspace, scope and applicable PRE/test/verify/POST gates. It MUST NOT require R04 completion, routing repair or routing PRE for unrelated UI artifacts. Dependencies SHALL follow actual consumed API/artifact/behavior; integration tasks MUST belong to the consumer. Shared-file merges SHALL preserve old evidence and domain invariants.
    26	
    27	#### Scenario: Parallel routing and UI work
    28	
    29	- **WHEN** UI and routing have isolated workspaces and independent behavior scopes
    30	- **THEN** each can advance through its own approved gates without acquiring a predecessor from the other program
    31	
    32	#### Scenario: Routing consumes UI artifacts
    33	
    34	- **WHEN** routing adopts UI tokens or independently approved shared-contract changes
    35	- **THEN** routing verifies its own integration/control tasks after supplier availability, and UI delivery does not wait for routing
    36	
    37	#### Scenario: New UI change
    38	
    39	- **WHEN** a new or modified UI change is reviewed after contract adoption
    40	- **THEN** absent rule/state/evidence mapping prevents a successful compliance verdict
    41	
    42	### Requirement: Shared component and workshop contract
    43	
    44	UI SHALL reuse semantic roles, the existing approved icon family and shared components. Each shared component SHALL describe anatomy, variants, sizes, states, keyboard, accessibility, tokens and examples. The workbench SHALL express personal ownership through real restored context, clear selection and factual persistence feedback. Unsupported operations MUST NOT appear functional.
    45	
    46	#### Scenario: Unimplemented AI provider
    47	
    48	- **WHEN** an AI representation is added without an approved provider integration
    49	- **THEN** its availability and behavior accurately identify the missing provider and no action claims data was sent or applied
    50	
    51	### Requirement: Checkpointed migration preserves semantics
    52	
    53	Each approved migration stage SHALL obtain PRE approval, actual required verification and independent POST approval before archival or a dependent implementation. Draw UI selection/theme feedback MUST NOT alter endpoints, routes, constraints, document semantics or repository flow ownership. A fixture archive MUST NOT be presented as a working installer.
    54	
    55	#### Scenario: Theme alters presentation
    56	
    57	- **WHEN** UI selection feedback or a palette changes around a diagram
    58	- **THEN** persisted diagram content, route constraints and repository contents remain identical
    59	
    60	#### Scenario: Required check cannot execute
    61	
    62	- **WHEN** a required accessibility or visual check cannot execute
    63	- **THEN** the report states BLOCKED or NOT_RUN with reason and the stage cannot claim PASS or advance

1	# ui-token-compliance Specification
     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	Provide executable evidence of semantic token integrity and enforce reviewable presentation rules in Frade's existing quality pipeline.
     6	
     7	## Requirements
     8	
     9	### Requirement: Deterministic token generation and contrast
    10	
    11	One versioned JSON token source SHALL generate all builtin CSS/typed role outputs deterministically. Light, Dark and HC SHALL have identical role sets. Drift, invalid source values or a failing named contrast pair MUST cause a nonzero check result. Checks MUST distinguish named-pair contrast from accessibility of the running application.
    12	
    13	#### Scenario: Manual generated output edit
    14	
    15	- **WHEN** a generated token file differs from regeneration
    16	- **THEN** the check fails without rewriting the evidence or output
    17	
    18	#### Scenario: Builtin token source
    19	
    20	- **WHEN** the canonical v1.0.0 source and generated outputs are checked
    21	- **THEN** all three palettes and 102 named contrast pairs pass independently of application visual approval
    22	
    23	### Requirement: Forced-colors precedence and exact adoption exception
    24	
    25	Generated CSS SHALL map every theme color role to its declared system keyword under forced-colors for root and inherited descendants with absent, System, Light, Dark and HC theme attributes under OS Light/Dark. The original input SHALL remain unchanged.
    26	
    27	#### Scenario: Automatic Dark with forced colors
    28	
    29	- **WHEN** OS prefers Dark, forced-colors is active and root has no theme attribute
    30	- **THEN** all generated theme roles resolve to the declared system keywords on root and inherited descendants
    31	
    32	#### Scenario: Explicit palette without forced colors
    33	
    34	- **WHEN** OS Light/Dark is active, forced-colors is inactive and a supported theme is selected
    35	- **THEN** the explicit palette remains unchanged; System and absent attribute follow OS preference
    36	
    37	#### Scenario: Unapproved second CSS deviation
    38	
    39	- **WHEN** generated CSS differs from the single-exception equivalence oracle in any other byte
    40	- **THEN** equivalence and drift checks fail without rewriting outputs or source evidence
    41	
    42	
    43	### Requirement: Exact single-selector CSS adoption boundary
    44	
    45	Frade CSS adoption revision 1 SHALL permit only the exact single selector replacement `:root:not([data-frade-theme])` → `:root:where(:not([data-frade-theme]))` in the automatic Dark media block. Every other source CSS byte, palette value, role and token version SHALL remain equivalent. Drift checks MUST reject any additional discrepancy.
    46	
    47	#### Scenario: Additional selector or token change is rejected
    48	
    49	- **WHEN** adopted generated CSS contains a discrepancy beyond the exact permitted selector replacement
    50	- **THEN** the unchanged equivalence and drift checks fail and preserve original source bytes
    51	
    52	
    53	### Requirement: Recorded adoption and actual cascade evidence
    54	
    55	Adoption revision/provenance SHALL be recorded separately from CSS bytes. Browser checks SHALL confirm requested media states and every role on root and an inherited child across the 20-state matrix; source named-pair checks alone MUST NOT claim cascade correctness.
    56	
    57	#### Scenario: Source contrast alone is insufficient for cascade acceptance
    58	
    59	- **WHEN** adoption provenance and browser cascade evidence are assessed
    60	- **THEN** provenance remains separate from CSS bytes and actual requested media states plus every root and inherited-child role are checked across the20-state matrix
    61	
    62	### Requirement: Feature literals and explicit exceptions
    63	
    64	New or changed feature presentation colors SHALL use semantic tokens. Validated theme data, approved brand data and persisted/domain diagram paint SHALL remain distinct permitted boundaries. Legacy exceptions SHALL identify exact occurrences, reasons and closure stages; they MUST NOT permit new literals in the same file.
    65	
    66	#### Scenario: Disallowed feature color
    67	
    68	- **WHEN** an isolated fixture adds a feature-level color literal
    69	- **THEN** the compliance check returns FAIL with its location
    70	
    71	#### Scenario: Declarative palette data
    72	
    73	- **WHEN** a valid theme fixture contains permitted HEX role data
    74	- **THEN** the theme boundary is accepted and unrelated feature literals remain checked
    75	
    76	### Requirement: Existing CI integration and honest enforcement
    77	
    78	UI compliance SHALL run in the real repository CI alongside retained project checks. A negative drift/literal control and a positive control SHALL execute outside production source and retain actual outcomes. Required branch checks SHALL be reported as configured only after authenticated remote verification; otherwise owner instructions and NOT_CONFIGURED or LOCAL_ONLY SHALL be provided.
    79	
    80	#### Scenario: Missing remote authority
    81	
    82	- **WHEN** branch rules cannot be verified or changed through an authorized authenticated mechanism
    83	- **THEN** the report records the limitation and never claims merge protection
    84	
    85	### Requirement: Fresh Git checkout preserves canonical LF bytes
    86	
    87	The root .gitattributes SHALL contain exactly the eight user-accepted logical entries in docs/ui/decisions/token-eol.gitattributes.proposed. A fresh Git checkout with temporary-repository core.autocrlf=true SHALL preserve all eight canonical artifact SHA256 hashes and LF bytes.
    88	
    89	#### Scenario: Windows-style checkout with accepted attributes
    90	
    91	- **WHEN** all eight protected artifacts are staged and freshly checked out with core.autocrlf=true and the exact accepted attribute entries
    92	- **THEN** all eight raw hashes match their original LF/UTF-8 bytes and the unchanged token checker exits 0 with 102 named pairs
    93	
    94	#### Scenario: Missing LF configuration reproduces drift
    95	
    96	- **WHEN** the isolated fixture freshly checks out the same artifacts with core.autocrlf=true and no LF attributes
    97	- **THEN** physical CRLF drift is observed and the unchanged token checker exits 1; canonical production/source/history files remain unchanged
    98	
    99	#### Scenario: Attribute scope broadening or retargeting
   100	
   101	- **WHEN** a required attribute entry is removed or an extra, wildcard or eol=crlf entry is supplied
   102	- **THEN** the checkout compliance check fails without changing the artifact byte oracle or automatically accepting new scope
   103	
   104	
   105	
   106	### Requirement: Checkout oracle and attribute scope stay strict
   107	
   108	The token checker and source-byte equivalence oracle MUST remain unchanged and MUST NOT normalize checked artifacts to hide CRLF drift. Only root configuration line separators may be normalized to compare its eight logical entries. Missing, extra, wildcard or CRLF-target rules MUST fail the checkout check.
   109	
   110	#### Scenario: Byte or attribute scope normalization is rejected
   111	
   112	- **WHEN** an artifact is normalized to hide CRLF drift or attribute entries are missing extra wildcard or CRLF-targeted
   113	- **THEN** the check fails while only root configuration line separators may be normalized for comparing eight logical entries
   114	
   115	
   116	### Requirement: Isolated checkout controls retain actual failures
   117	
   118	Controls SHALL execute in a verified OS-temp Git repository using existing Node/Git, retain actual exit/hash evidence and safely remove that isolated root. Missing Git or failed cleanup MUST NOT count as PASS or skipped coverage.
   119	
   120	#### Scenario: Git or fixture cleanup fails
   121	
   122	- **WHEN** the verified OS-temp checkout control cannot execute Git or cannot safely remove its owned root
   123	- **THEN** actual failure and exit/hash evidence remain recorded and coverage is neither skipped nor reported PASS
   124	
   125	
   126	### Requirement: Checkout implementation preserves independent review origin
   127	
   128	Focused independent PRE MUST approve the added path before production implementation; prior review evidence MUST remain immutable.
   129	
   130	#### Scenario: Checkout implementation path is introduced
   131	
   132	- **WHEN** the added checkout path is proposed for production implementation
   133	- **THEN** focused independent PRE precedes implementation and earlier review evidence remains immutable
   134	
   135	### Requirement: UI compliance survives specification archival
   136	
   137	UI compliance SHALL read a stable canonical BDD contract independent of the active OpenSpec change directory. Archiving or removing the completed change artifact SHALL preserve successful binding/control execution. Missing or malformed canonical BDD MUST fail rather than fall back to an active/archive copy.
   138	
   139	#### Scenario: Completed change is archived
   140	
   141	- **WHEN** an isolated fixture moves the active change into archive
   142	- **THEN** actual traceability CLI and compliance controls still pass against the unchanged canonical BDD contract
   143	
   144	#### Scenario: Active and archive artifacts are absent
   145	
   146	- **WHEN** an isolated fixture contains canonical docs/registry/assertion sources but no active or archived change
   147	- **THEN** actual runtime checks still pass without consulting OpenSpec lifecycle state
   148	
   149	#### Scenario: Canonical contract is missing or malformed
   150	
   151	- **WHEN** canonical BDD is missing or malformed while a historical change copy still exists
   152	- **THEN** compliance fails without fallback, suppressed errors, skipped tests or a rewritten baseline
   153	
   154	
   155	### Requirement: Archive-safe compliance retains strict controls and durable links
   156	
   157	Existing foundation assertions, explicit future boundaries, token/literal negatives and immutable historical evidence MUST remain strict. Owner instruction links SHALL point to durable documentation.
   158	
   159	#### Scenario: Owner follows compliance instructions after archival
   160	
   161	- **WHEN** a completed change is archived and its compliance instructions are used
   162	- **THEN** links lead to durable documentation and foundation assertions future boundaries token/literal negatives and historical evidence remain strict and unchanged

    43	## Requirements
    44	
    45	### Requirement: Builtin themes and independent density
    46	
    47	The first runtime release SHALL provide offline Light, Dark and HC together, default System, explicit theme priority and independent compact/comfortable persistent density; forced-colors MUST remain system-controlled.
    48	
    49	#### Scenario: Explicit Light and OS Dark
    50	
    51	- **WHEN** the OS changes to Dark after explicit Light selection
    52	- **THEN** Light remains selected and density/settings are preserved
    53	
    54	### Requirement: Deterministic complete resolution
    55	
    56	Resolution SHALL preserve immutable source data, fill every registered role, apply declared override precedence and validate named contrast pairs. External low-contrast roles SHALL repair deterministically with diagnostics, bounded ten passes and builtin fallback on nonconvergence.
    57	
    58	#### Scenario: Low contrast theme
    59	
    60	- **WHEN** an external palette violates a named pair
    61	- **THEN** resolution returns a valid repaired or full builtin snapshot and identifies repaired roles
    62	
    63	### Requirement: Atomic hot preview and commit
    64	
    65	All required presentation participants SHALL apply one revision without restart. Preview MUST NOT persist. Cancellation or adapter/persistence failure SHALL restore the previous snapshot and settings without losing dirty editors, selections, undo or document bytes. Stale candidate results MUST NOT overwrite newer selection.
    66	
    67	#### Scenario: Canvas preparation fails
    68	
    69	- **WHEN** a required adapter refuses the preview or commit
    70	- **THEN** all participants/settings remain at the previous theme and documents are unchanged
    71	
    72	### Requirement: Measurable UI coverage
    73	
    74	P01 SHALL verify Light/Dark/HC × both densities, keyboard picker, forced-colors/coarse/reduced-motion and state preservation on actual runtime screens. A p95 hot-apply budget of 150 ms SHALL be measured on identified hardware/workspace after package load; missing measurements MUST NOT be reported as PASS.
    75	
    76	#### Scenario: Rapid A B C selection
    77	
    78	- **WHEN** older theme preparation completes after C
    79	- **THEN** C remains committed with no partial participant revision or late setting write
    80	
    81	### Requirement: Presentation consumer isolation
    82	
    83	Theme changes SHALL affect view presentation only. Persisted JSON/XML, authored page/background images/node/edge paint, route/endpoint semantics, model state, undo/redo, selection and editor/graph/iframe identity MUST remain unchanged. No theme transaction SHALL invoke persisted background/grid convenience APIs or trigger autosave/settings preference writes.
    84

    86	- **WHEN** a dirty native and pinned embedded diagram with nondefault authored paint previews, commits, cancels and redraws under forced colors
    87	- **THEN** saved document bytes, settings storage, model/undo/selection/identities stay unchanged while only UI view projection follows the current theme
    88

    90	- **WHEN** a foreign source/origin or obsolete frame generation sends an acknowledgement

    94

1	# workbench-visual-contract Specification
     2	
     3	## Purpose
     4	
     5	Define a reviewable successor visual contract for migrated workbench surfaces without silently replacing the existing approved VS Code pilot.
     6	
     7	The user accepted the full WB-001 replacement text on 30 September 2026. The canonical accepted text is in `../../decisions/visual-contract.md`; authority, text hash and explicit supersession ownership are in `../../decisions/wb001-acceptance-2026-09-30.md`. The pilot archive/sync owner consumes that record; this change does not edit/archive the pilot. Acceptance does not approve migration baselines or replace independent PRE.
     8	
     9	## Archive provenance
    10	
    11	The Purpose above is preserved verbatim from the accepted delta. Its source-relative inline paths refer to the original change. Current canonical authority: [accepted WB-001 text](../../changes/archive/2026-09-30-frade-ui-design-contract/decisions/visual-contract.md) and [acceptance and successor ownership](../../changes/archive/2026-09-30-frade-ui-design-contract/decisions/wb001-acceptance-2026-09-30.md).
    12	
    13	## Requirements
    14	
    15	### Requirement: Explicit accepted visual transition
    16	
    17	An approved decision SHALL reconcile pilot WB-001 ownership before migrated surfaces use Frade guide v1.0 instead of exact VS Code Dark Modern colors/geometry. Non-migrated surfaces SHALL retain their existing contracts. Behavioral workbench requirements, diagram compatibility and historical evidence SHALL remain intact. A proposal or token PASS MUST NOT be treated as acceptance of visual migration.
    18	
    19	#### Scenario: Proposed palette conflict
    20	
    21	- **WHEN** the guide requires graphite/light/HC colors and dimensions differing from the pinned pilot
    22	- **THEN** the exact conflict and complete replacement decision are reviewed before implementation or baseline acceptance
    23	
    24	### Requirement: Measurable stage evidence

Реальная обязательность: компонентный слой + lint/CI + защищённые branch checks + reviewers. Для локального режима без CI gate исполняется локально и его отчёт сохраняется; статус `LOCAL_ONLY` MUST быть виден, автоматическую защиту ветки утверждать нельзя.
   338	
   339	### 14.1 UI compliance gate
   340	
   341	| Проверка | PASS требует |
   342	|---|---|
   343	| Scope | Изменения укладываются в разрешённые пути и approved contract. |
   344	| Tokens | Нет новых feature-level цветовых литералов; generated CSS соответствует JSON; проверенные пары проходят контраст. |
   345	| Components | Переиспользование shared UI либо описанный новый контракт; нет второй визуальной системы. |
   346	| States | Проверены все затронутые состояния, включая ошибки/dirty/loading при наличии. |
   347	| Keyboard | Можно пройти основной сценарий и выйти/отменить без мыши. |
   348	| A11y | Нет относящихся к изменению нарушений обязательных правил; применимые исключения документированы. |
   349	| Visual | Light/dark/high contrast и compact/comfortable для изменённых экранов; отсутствие clipping при resize/zoom. |
   350	| Regression | Не изменены данные/dirty-state при навигации; обязательные проектные тесты пройдены. |
   351	| Evidence | Реальные результаты с датой, окружением, командами, commit и ограничениями. |
   352	
   353	Только шесть фотографий разных тем не заменяют проверку поведения. Если инструменты недоступны — указать BLOCKED или NOT_RUN для соответствующей проверки; не придумывать успешные результаты.
   354	
   355	### 14.2 Изменение правил и исключения
   356	
   357	Новые оттенки, токены, варианты или паттерны сначала описываются в общем слое и документе. ADR содержит проблему, рассмотренные варианты, принятое правило, затронутые IDs, область, проверку и миграцию. Routine выбор значения из существующих токенов не требует отдельного разрешения пользователя.
   358	
   359	Исключение из MUST допустимо только через принятое изменение самой спецификации в действующем workflow; временное исключение имеет owner, причину, срок/этап закрытия и scope. Слова «так красивее» или «модель предложила» не являются обоснованием. Изменение лого согласуется с бренд-контрактом; стайл-гайд не создаёт новую версию бренда молча.
   360	
   361	Версии: patch — уточнение текста; minor — совместимый новый компонент/роль; major — изменение существующего поведения/токен-контракта с планом миграции. Версия фиксируется в guide, JSON и evidence. UI-owner/reviewer — роль, назначаемая в реальном проекте, а не выдуманное имя.
   362	
   363	## 15. BDD/TDD для внедрения
   364	
   365	BDD-контракты приведены в `ui-contracts.feature`. Они покрывают тему, плотность, фокус, клавиатуру, dirty tabs, LoV, flow detach, standalone/bound и AI. Файл — спецификация, не исполняемый тест без step definitions и adapter реального приложения.

   605	function uiContrast(foreground: string, background: string): number {
   606	  const luminance = (value: string) => {
   607	    const rgb = value
   608	      .match(/[\d.]+/g)

   610	      .map(Number)

   614	      .map((value) => (value <= 0.04045 ? value / 12.92 : ((value + 0.055) / 1.055) ** 2.4))

**PRE review fails on two blockers. No production work is authorized by this review.**

1. **The registry plan conflicts with unchanged tests.** Main and the renderer both call the default `createThemeRegistry()`; the plan adds the reference theme there so the picker and startup can see it ([design.md](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/openspec/changes/frade-vscode-dark-2026/design.md:25)). Existing tests require that registry to list exactly three built-ins and the picker to show exactly four options including System ([resolver.test.ts](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/packages/ui-workspace/tests/ui-contract/resolver.test.ts:15), [picker.test.tsx](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/packages/ui-workspace/tests/ui-contract/picker.test.tsx:177)). The allowed paths prohibit changing those assertions ([design.md](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/openspec/changes/frade-vscode-dark-2026/design.md:36)). Reconcile the registration approach and test scope explicitly, preserving the built-in guarantees, then revalidate the plan before another PRE.

2. **Relevant packet inputs are missing.** The renderer imports `apps/desktop/src/renderer/style.css`, which is needed to assess the actual cascade and geometry ([main.tsx](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/apps/desktop/src/renderer/main.tsx:8)). The packet also omits the current legacy-color inventory and UI/P01 traceability mappings read by mandatory compliance checks ([colors.mjs](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/scripts/ui/colors.mjs:150), [traceability.mjs](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/scripts/ui/traceability.mjs:167), [p01.bdd.test.tsx](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/packages/ui-workspace/tests/ui-contract/p01.bdd.test.tsx:61)). Include them in a fresh immutable packet; local strict validation does not replace independent review of these inputs.

The user’s `gpt-6-sol/xhigh` PRE choice is supported by the authority record and plan table ([user-authority.json](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/openspec/changes/frade-vscode-dark-2026/evidence/planning-20261025/user-authority.json:3), [design.md](/mnt/e/dev/codex/frade/.git/frade-workflow/runs/2026-10-25T16-36-04-325Z-ba258180-a560-4dff-903c-997d38cf2fbb/prepared/packet/openspec/changes/frade-vscode-dark-2026/design.md:15)).
